sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Physical Arbitrage of Grade A Refined Copper Cathodes

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law framework with corporate law historically inspired by the General Corporation Law of Delaware)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (entered into force 2012)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of April 27, 2015, as amended, establishing the AML/CFT legal framework; Executive Decree No. 400 of 2015 implementing regulations; Cabinet Decree No. 21 of August 3, 2020, creating the Uniform Beneficial Ownership Registry; DGI Resolution No. 124 of 2020 on beneficial ownership reporting; Law 52 of October 27, 2016, immobilizing bearer shares.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Panamanian incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the beneficial owner's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of the ultimate beneficial owner and directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing government authority of the holder's nationality

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate or equivalent background check of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or competent criminal record authority in the UBO's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming the UBO's financial standing and source of funds
Affidavit of Beneficial Ownership (Declaración Jurada de Beneficiario Final)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian notary public and corporate agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization, no consular legalization required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all incorporators, UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK OFSI Consolidated List, and Panama's National Designated Persons List. Both automated World-Check or equivalent database checks and manual adverse-media review must be completed. Positive PEP hits require enhanced due diligence and senior management approval under Law 23 of 2015. Any sanction match triggers a frozen-file protocol and suspicious transaction report to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá) – Online Name Clearance and Reservation System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed corporate names may use English or Spanish, but all names must be rendered in Latin characters. Non-Latin names must be transliterated according to official Spanish orthographic rules. The name must end with a corporate suffix such as 'S.A.', 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', or 'LLC', with 'S.A.' being standard. Accented vowels and ñ are permitted only where required; all other special characters and punctuation are disallowed. The name must not be identical or phonetically confusingly similar to any existing registered entity, foundation, or trademark recorded in the Public Registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within five business days of an official name rejection notice, the corporate agent may file a written Recurso de Apelación with the Dirección General de Registro of the Public Registry. The appeal must restate the proposed name, attach the denial certificate, and include a legal memorandum demonstrating distinguishability or, where similarity is alleged, an express written consent from the prior registrant. The Registry will issue a resolution within fifteen business days from the filing date. If the appeal is rejected, the applicant may submit a wholly new name application through the same online portal without further appeal rights.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for general corporate compliance; the Public Registry and Dirección General de Impuestos (DGI) accept the registered agent's physical address as the statutory registered office. However, for an active wholesale copper cathode trading company engaged in documentary LC and LME warrant transfers, banks and counterparties generally require evidence of physical substance, such as a service-address agreement, leased office, or local administrative facility. A purely virtual office may satisfy corporate law but carries elevated risk of bank refusal or enhanced due diligence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for the Public Registry (less than 5% annual probability for a standard S.A.); moderate for financial institutions engaged in enhanced due diligence (approximately 10–15% during the onboarding phase for base-metals trading); unannounced physical inspections become more likely if the UAF or the Superintendency of Banks issues an administrative order based on a triggering event.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name clearance and reservation fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory tariff (Arancel del Registro Público)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation (Pacto Social)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary tariff plus prevailing market fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registry inscription fee for the incorporation deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration tariff based on corporate capital (no minimum capital required)
DGI fixed administrative fee for UBO register submission

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent and registered office for the first fiscal year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian resident agent (law firm or trust company)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard S.A. maintenance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille of UBO identity and background documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Source country competent authority (e.g., Apostille office) and Panamanian notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular / apostille fees plus messenger and translation costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening package for all UBOs and directors
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per individual screened (OFAC, UN, UK, EU, Panama lists)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation due diligence and corporate drafting (legal opinion, corporate records binder, statutory ledger setup)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional hourly fee and fixed drafting fee for standard S.A. setup

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Panama General Corporation Law — Ley 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927, as amended by Ley 5 de 2008 and Ley 20 de 2013; Articles 1–52 (formation, capital structure, corporate governance); Article 10 (required clauses of the articles of incorporation); Article 24 (board of directors); Article 39 (resident agent obligation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil (Mercantile Division of the Public Registry of Panama), Panama City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Pacto Social y Estatutos) — Public Notarial Deed of Incorporation, registered as the 'Inscripción de Sociedad Anónima'.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow requirement. The authorized capital is typically fixed at US$10,000 represented by shares of US$1.00 par value (or no-par shares); shares may be issued fully paid against cash or other lawful consideration, and no deposit or escrow with a Panamanian bank is mandated by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS ADOPTED AT THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], S.A., HELD IN PANAMA CITY ON [DATE]. FIRST: The directors ratify the subscription of ten thousand (10,000) common shares of par value one dollar (US$1.00) each, representing the entire authorized capital, issued fully paid against shareholder contributions without escrow. SECOND: The registered office is established at [ADDRESS], Corregimiento de [X], District of Panama, Republic of Panama, and the resident agent appointment is confirmed. THIRD: [NAME] is appointed President, [NAME] Secretary, and [NAME] Treasurer, each accepting the office. FOURTH: The President and Treasurer, jointly, are authorized to open corporate banking accounts and execute routine transactions for the wholesale trading of Grade A copper cathodes. APPROVED unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección de Registro de Personas (name-search window) or online via PanamaTramite.gob.pa portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the official name search application listing three proposed corporate names in order of preference. Pay the search fee at the Registry cashier. On approval, obtain the Certificate of Name Availability, which reserves the name for 30 days and blocks registration of a similar name by a third party.
required_dossiers: Completed Solicitud de Búsqueda de Nombre (name search form)
Copy of applicant passport or cédula
Fee payment receipt (Registry stamp fees)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry rejects a name for being identical or confusingly similar to an existing company, apply for reconsideration in writing within five days; alternatively, submit two new alternative names and pay a new search fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Articles of Incorporation (Pacto Social) Before a Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública del Circuito de Panamá (Panamanian notary); notaries operate under the supervision of the Corte Suprema de Justicia – Sala de Negocios Generales.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct corporate counsel to prepare the Pacto Social and Estatutos containing the corporate name, registered office address, corporate object (wholesale physical trading of Grade A refined copper cathodes and other non-ferrous metals, ISIC 4662), authorized capital, term, governance clauses, and appointment of the Resident Agent (a licensed Panamanian attorney or law firm). At least two incorporators execute the deed before the notary, who authenticates signatures and issues the testimonio (certified first copy) for submission to the Registry.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation with Estatutos
Certificate of Name Availability
Passports or cédulas of incorporators and initial directors
Resident Agent acceptance letter from the appointed Panamanian law firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a formal deficiency (e.g., missing statutory clause or witness), correct the draft and re-execute the deed by addendum (copia adicionada) before the testing notary; obtain a fresh testimonio for filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Registration at the Mercantile Division of the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil (Avenida Samuel Lewis, Panama City) or the PANATRAMITE online filing module.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized testimonio of the incorporation deed, the name reservation certificate, and the official registry fee payment. The Registry examiner verifies compliance with Ley 32, assigns the Ficha (corporate registration number), and issues the 'Inscripción de Sociedad Anónima'. An optional 24-hour expedited review is available for a surcharge.
required_dossiers: Original testimonio of the public deed of incorporation
Certificate of Name Availability
Proof of payment of registry fees (approximately US$500 per official tariff schedule)
Cover letter from the resident agent law firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the examiner issues a defect report, the resident agent files a 'subsanación' (defect cure) within ten business days; for substantive defects, execute a corrective public deed and re-file. If the cure period lapses, the application is archived and a new filing with fees is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the Corporate Existence Record and Personería Jurídica
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección de Registro (same Registry, certification desk).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the registration, the Registry generates the electronic Ficha and the certified registration extract. The company evidences its legal personality through a certified 'Certificado de Registro' or an updated Ficha. For cross-border banking, request an Apostille on the certificate of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Registration control number and receipt
Request form for certified corporate certificate (Formulario de Solicitud de Certificado)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Clerical or data-entry errors in the Ficha are corrected through a motion of 'Aclaración' filed at the same Registry; no notarial re-execution is required for typographical corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Adoption of the Pro-Forma Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Board of Directors (private internal act); notarization and official minutes prepared by the corporate secretary for bank and DGI use.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the initial directors named in the articles and adopt the First Board Resolution covering share subscription, adoption of the registered office, appointment of officers, and banking authorization. Record the resolution in the corporate minute book (Libro de Actas), have it certified by the Secretary, and prepare notarized copies for the bank KYC file and the RUC process at the DGI.
required_dossiers: Draft First Board Resolution
Corporate minute book (opened and foliated)
Signed acceptance letters from appointed officers
Notarized copy of the deed and Ficha
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum is not achieved, re-notice the meeting in accordance with the bylaws; in lieu of dissent, record the dissenting director's position and proceed by majority; alternatively, adopt the resolution by unanimous written consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Municipal Operating Notice (RUC / Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, via the SIF e-filing platform; Municipality of Panama – Department of Aviso de Operación / Patente.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the RUC application with the DGI within one month of the deed execution, selecting territorial taxation (Panama-source income only) and the ISIC 4662 wholesale metals activity code; obtain the RUC number. Then file the municipal Aviso de Operación and pay the patent fee based on declared capital; receive the Certificado de Aviso de Operación for the registered office address. No sector-specific statutory license is required for wholesale copper trading.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the incorporation Ficha
DGI RUC application form (Formulario RUC-1)
Certified First Board Resolution appointing officers
Identity cards (cédulas/passports) of the legal representative
Lease agreement or evidence of title for the registered office premises
Municipal Aviso de Operación application and payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI rejects the application due to an incorrect activity code, correct the SIF record through the RUC amendment module; if the Municipalidad rejects the Aviso due to zoning, submit the certificate of property use (Certificado de Uso de Suelo) and appeal the administrative denial before the Juzgado Municipal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Comercio (no sectoral manufacturing or import/export license is mandated for wholesale physical trading of refined non-ferrous metals under ISIC 4662).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Aviso de Operación y Patente Municipal (general commercial operating permit); optional Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas bonded-warehouse license if the company elects to operate its own copper cathode storage terminal.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Registration — pure office-based wholesale trading does not require an EIA study under Ley 41 de 1998 and Decreto Ejecutivo 123 de 2009 (EIA Regulation, as updated by Resolución DM-0264-2010); a Category II Environmental Registration is triggered only if the company adds a physical storage yard or warehouse exceeding 1,000 m² or handling controlled waste streams.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or emission sources for office-based trading operations. If warehousing is added: comply with the Panamanian wastewater technical standard DGNTI-COPANIT 35-2000 for discharges to the public sewer; manage solid waste under Ley 38 de 2008 (General Solid Waste Law); keep cathode stock dunnage and sweepings covered to prevent particulate release; any secondary copper processing or smelting would raise the classification to Category I requiring a full EIA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office premises require a fire safety inspection certificate from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; occupational health clearance is issued by the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) pursuant to the OHS regulations and the General Labor Law; if storage racking is installed, a structural load certificate from the Municipality must be obtained; for pure office trading, the standard occupancy certificate (Certificado de Uso de Suelo) suffices.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Republic of Panama; official online taxpayer portal: E-Tax (Panama's DGI electronic tax administration system).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an active Sociedad Anónima: DGI issues the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) upon application filed by the company's resident agent or accredited legal representative through the E-Tax portal, accompanied by the public deed of incorporation, last corporate registry certificate, and identification documents of directors and officers. A non-resident shareholder need not appear in person. Where the S.A. is not yet in taxable activity, no RUC is required; the RUC becomes mandatory when the company commences Panama-source or export activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election is available. Under the Código Fiscal, an S.A. is automatically an entity-level corporate taxpayer for all Panama-source income. No pass-through status is elective. Special tax regimes such as SEM (Sede de Empresa Multinacional), Colon Free Zone, or free-zone licences are separate statutory concessions, not entity classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Corporales Muebles y Servicios) — Panamanian value-added tax on goods and services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold in Balboa/USD; any person making taxable transfers or providing taxable services in Panamanian territory must register for RUC/ITBMS before commencing activities. The 'pequeño contribuyente' simplified fixed-tax regime is a limited domestic small-business scheme and does not constitute a general registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory DGI-authorised electronic invoicing (facturación electrónica) through E-Tax; taxpayers must transmit canonical XML with digital signature for each invoice. DGI validates the transaction and returns a Código de Autorización (authorization code) functioning as a real-time fiscal clearance stamp. Export invoices must reference the SIGA customs export declaration and must be issued with ITBMS at 0%.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% ITBMS applies to tangible goods, including copper cathodes, physically exported from Panamanian customs territory, to re-exports from Colon Free Zone or other free zones, and to ancillary freight or logistics services directly connected to exports. Pure offshore LME warrant transactions in which the goods never enter Panamanian territory and title passes outside Panama are outside the territorial tax base and require no Panama export documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged in SIGA (Sistema Integrado de Gestión Aduanera)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill (original negotiable or certified copy)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank certificate of receipt of export proceeds in Panama)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and Panama customs co-ordinate audits of SIGA export declarations, export invoices, and FX remittance records. Missing or inconsistent documentation is treated as evidence of a domestic sale and may trigger retroactive 7% ITBMS assessment plus statutory interest, surcharges, and fines. Fraudulent zero-rating claims may give rise to criminal tax exposure and suspension of the exporter's RUC and E-Tax electronic invoice authorisation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) — the Republic of Panama maintains no central bank and no separate foreign-exchange administration; the SBP acts as the prudential supervisor of banks, trust-service providers, and custody institutions, while the United States Federal Reserve functions as the de facto monetary anchor via full dollarization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Free and complete convertibility across both current and capital accounts. The Panamanian Balboa (PAB) circulates only as coins at a fixed 1:1 parity with the US Dollar, which is legal tender for all transactions. Panama imposes no exchange permits, no prior licensing for inbound or outbound wires, and no restriction on profit remittance, dividend distribution, interest payments, or liquidation proceeds payable to non-resident shareholders. The only operational constraint is bank-level AML/CFT reporting: transactions equaling or exceeding USD 10,000 must be evidenced with supporting documentation, and any flow that triggers the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) threshold requires a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR). For a copper-cathode arbitrage company, where goods move from a foreign supplier to a foreign buyer without entering Panamanian customs territory, the resulting margin is foreign-source income under Panama's territorial tax model; therefore the repatriation runway for commercial margin and invested capital is entirely unrestricted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama applies no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory repatriation timeline, and no forced conversion ratio for export proceeds because export receipts are invoiced and settled in US Dollars. A copper-trading S.A. holding an operational account with an SBP-licensed bank may retain 100% of export proceeds onshore or offshore without conversion. The only compliance duty is traceability: each receipt must match a valid commercial transaction under Decree Law 2 of 2008 and Law 23 of 2015, evidenced by the commercial invoice, LME warrant transfer, bill of lading, and the corresponding SWIFT MT103 reference.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Impuesto Anual de Sociedades / Tasa Única)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before March 15; payable each calendar year by all active Panamanian S.A. corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% surcharge on the USD 300 annual tax plus statutory interest accrual; non-payment for two consecutive years permits the Registro Público to treat the corporation as 'omissa' and administrative strike-off after the third consecutive year

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year the deadline is March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines under the Código Fiscal, late-payment interest on tax due, and additional recargos; persistent non-filing can trigger coercive collection and administrative penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (Declaración Anual de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Registro de Beneficiarios Finales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days after the entity anniversary date in the Beneficial Ownership Registry; separate enrollment required within 30 days after incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update the declaration subjects the corporation to monetary fines per day of delay, including possible suspension of corporate rights or prohibitions on certain acts with the Registro Público until the filing is cured

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent certified audit is required when annual gross income or annual taxable income exceeds USD 1,000,000; banks, insurance companies, licensed financial entities, and issuers of publicly traded securities are required to file audited financial statements regardless of size
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by the Colegio de Contadores Públicos Autorizados de Panamá; smaller entities may apply the IFRS for SMEs framework

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every Panamanian S.A. must maintain updated beneficial ownership data and file an annual confirmatory declaration with the Beneficial Ownership Registry within 30 days of each registration anniversary. Shareholding transfers occurring during the year must be reflected in the declaration at the next annual update, and any material change in ultimate beneficial control must be notified prior to the annual cycle if required by DGI regulations
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (applies to taxable income above USD 1,500,000; progressive 5% and 15% brackets apply below USD 50,000 and between USD 50,000 and USD 1,500,000 respectively)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial source exclusion: trading margins from copper cathode sales negotiated, executed and settled wholly outside Panama are exempt from Panamanian CIT; new corporations pay 50% of the statutory rates for the first two fiscal years, capping the effective Panama-source rate at 12.5%; qualifying Multinational Headquarters (SEM) companies may elect the 5% special regime; Colon Free Zone operators benefit from reduced 2.5%-5% rates on re-export margins

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 100 (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta) filed through the DGI e-Tax portal (e-Tax 5.0 / Mis Cuentas T@x); transfer-pricing annex attached to the same filing when related-party transactions exceed USD 250,000
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return; monthly advance payments (pagos fraccionados) and monthly withholding returns are due during the fiscal year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within three months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year companies the deadline is 31 March of the following year; no general extension is available

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name, NIT/RUC tax identification number, registered office, resident agent details and ISIC activity code 4662 (wholesale of non-ferrous copper cathodes)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only the Panamanian S.A. legal identifiers; a 100% non-resident owned company files under its own NIT and must never list foreign shareholders on the tax declaration

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross Panama-source income, including trading margins and commissions where negotiation, order execution and invoicing occur in Panama
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude extraterritorial copper trades where title passes outside Panama; retain LME warrant transfers, bills of lading and documentary LC records proving foreign source

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales returns, discounts and rebates deductible from gross income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Substantiate any chargebacks with dated credit notes; receivables held by foreign shareholders abroad should not generate deductions on the Panama return

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net gross Panama-source income after returns and discounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This figure must reconcile to the statutory books; artificial gross-up or under-aging of foreign margins triggers territory audit exposure

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of copper cathode sales, freight, insurance, brokerage, financing costs and transfer-pricing adjustments; deductions require supporting invoices and satisfy the causal relation test
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to foreign related suppliers must be arm's length benchmarked and supported by a transfer-pricing file; expenses to non-resident holding companies require withholding proof and substance evidence

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net income after offset of tax losses absorbed within the five-year carryforward window (Law 134 of 2023 regime)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only previously assessed Panama-source losses may be applied; losses generated by extraterritorial copper operations are not deductible

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT computed at the 5%/15%/25% progressive brackets on the taxable base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 50% rate reduction for the first two fiscal years where the S.A. filed a start-of-operations notice and genuinely commenced Panama-source activity

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 112 - Pagos fraccionados, retenciones y saldo
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of monthly advance payments, withholding tax credits and the resulting balance payable or carried forward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Monthly advance payments are mandatory even for non-resident owned companies; non-payment attracts surcharges independent of the final-year reconciliation

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge on the tax due (minimum USD 100), monthly interest at 1%, and an administrative fine up to USD 500; persistent non-filing enables DGI estimated assessment, asset seizure and criminal tax evasion prosecution under the Penal Code and Law 134 of 2023

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% on dividends distributed out of profits already taxed under Panamanian CIT; 10% on dividends paid from untaxed or exempt earnings, including foreign-source margins; no withholding applies to capital redemptions below paid-in capital
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama applies DTAs signed with Singapore, UAE, Korea, Mexico, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Spain, Portugal, Italy and Barbados, among others. To invoke relief the receiving shareholder must (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its jurisdiction of residence, (2) legalize or apostille the TRC and file it together with a certified beneficial-ownership statement with the paying Panamanian S.A., and (3) instruct the S.A. to apply the reduced treaty rate at the moment of distribution; the DGI may require supplementary substance evidence before honoring a lower rate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties, technical assistance and IP licensing paid to non-residents: statutory 12.5% withholding, generally reduced to 5%-10% under an applicable DTA; interest paid to non-resident lenders: statutory 6% withholding (exempt for interest on registered bonds), commonly reduced to 5% under treaty; payments to related parties in zero or low-tax jurisdictions are reviewed for substance and arm's length character

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD/PAB 250,000 aggregate related-party cross-border transactions in a fiscal year; this threshold also triggers the mandatory transfer-pricing annex to Formulario 100 and the preparation of Local File and Master File where either related-party transactions exceed USD/PAB 250,000 or gross income exceeds USD/PAB 3,000,000
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not maintain a Gulf-style ESR, but the territorial system itself demands an economic activity analysis: only margins produced by functions, assets and risks located in Panama are taxed. Law 134 of 2023 inserted a general anti-avoidance clause allowing the DGI to recharacterize transactions lacking business purpose and to disregard shell companies; a copper-trading S.A. must evidence real board meetings in Panama, a resident agent, substantive bank accounts, and documented negotiation, invoicing and risk decisions, otherwise the foreign-source exemption is denied and the entire margin is reassessed as Panama-source

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-declaring Panama-source copper trading margins, artificially allocating profits abroad, or submitting a forged Formulario 100 to reduce the CIT liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud sanctioned by up to six years imprisonment and fines of multiples of the evaded tax; administrative surcharge of 10% and monthly interest of 1%; DGI asset seizure after final assessment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing false declarations or approving fictitious invoicing are jointly liable for the defrauded tax, face civil restitution, prohibition to leave Panama (travel ban), disqualification from board positions, and imprisonment as co-authors

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominee-owned Panama S.A. lacking office, staff, bank activity or resident-agent substance to route copper cathode transactions and claim the foreign-source exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI recharacterizes the entity, assesses the full trading margin as Panama-source CIT, adds 1% monthly interest and penalties; the S.A. may be flagged as an 'empresa fantasma' and struck from the Public Registry
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee and front directors are personally assessed for unpaid tax and can be prosecuted under Law 23 of 2015 for facilitating fraud; personal bank accounts and assets are subject to freezing orders and travel bans
